Camera is CRITICALLY a HIGH FRONT-ABOVE CAMERA, looking steeply DOWN about50degrees toward her chest and waist. Front direction nearly square to the body, only a very small oblique offset to her anatomical RIGHT. It must clearly show the TOP of her head, shoulders and the horizontal plane of the forearm, NOT a near-eye-level photograph. Use perspective with natural proportions, no fisheye. The hand is farther forward than her torso, thumb pointing up, wrist neutral, relaxed fingers. Upper arm remains down, elbow touching side. The other LEFT arm on imageRIGHT hangs naturally beside thigh, no assisting contact.
Key geometry: right elbow beside waist is fixed anchor; midpoint forearm goes forward/toward viewer and down image, external rotation later goes outward toward imageLEFT, internal rotation later lies across belly toward imageRIGHT. The three directions must be readable in this high front-above projection. Do not show internal rotation already in midpoint.
